thread:
maya_cs: FYI — spotted odd churn in healthscore for a subset of trials: scores flipflopping between 28 and 52 over a few minutes. Affects renewal queues.
eli_data: can you drop a couple sample accounts?
maya_cs: acct_r7h2, acct_q5m9, acct_u3p4 — saw two different healthscore rows within 7 min for same account
toni_eng: paste the log snippet if you have it
maya_cs: logs:
```
2026-10-11T10:14:01Z healthscore.compute account=acct_r7h2 run=run_x01 params=hs_v5 cache_hit=true score=52
2026-10-11T10:17:03Z healthscore.compute account=acct_r7h2 run=run_x02 params=hs_v5 cache_hit=false score=28
```
eli_data: running quick aggregation to find oscillators:
```
SELECT account_id, array_agg(score ORDER BY ts) AS scores, count(*) as events
FROM healthscore_events
WHERE ts >= '2026-10-11'
GROUP BY account_id
HAVING max(score) - min(score) > 20
LIMIT 50;
```
eli_data: returned 31 accounts matching pattern, most with cache_hit toggles and playbook re-evals within minutes
sam_ops: any recent deploys to runner or cache? could be a TTL/consistency edge
toni_eng: we rolled out cache-shard affinity change yesterday to reduce cross-AZ reads. I wonder if stale cached partial results + concurrent webhook-driven re-evals could cause an older partial score to write over a fresh one
eli_data: correlation looks like this: webhook from CRM updates last_activity -> triggers immediate health re-eval (bypasses cache), but the queued async batch re-eval (older job) later writes cached score to the same account, overwriting the immediate one
maya_cs: consequence: customers toggled in/out of at-risk lists, renewals queue jittered. Some reps got duplicate pings when score changed back to high-risk
toni_eng: mitigation proposal:
1) make healthscore writes idempotent using versioning (write only if compute_ts >= stored_compute_ts)
2) pause automated outbound sends for accounts that flip >once in 15m
3) short-term: increase cache write TTL jitter to avoid deterministic overwrite
sam_ops: I like the version guard. Short-term I'd also add a dedupe key to playbook-runner for health_recalc runs keyed by account + compute_id
playbook-bot: scheduled toggle for pb_health_recalc.dedupe_rule at 2026-10-11T10:30:00Z (job id job_90090)
toni_eng: I'll push a hotfix to the write-path to check stored_compute_ts before overwriting. Also will add a metric for "health_write_overwrites" to detect future regressions
eli_data: exporting affected accounts CSV to s3://redwood-cs-temp/oscillators_2945123456.csv
eli_data: link: s3://redwood-cs-temp/oscillators_2945123456.csv
maya_cs: please also suppress tmpl_renewal_alert outbound for these accounts until we reconcile
crm-bot: created suppressor for template=tmpl_renewal_alert account_list=s3://redwood-cs-temp/oscillators_2945123456.csv active=true until=2026-10-11T18:00:00Z
sam_ops: adding monitor: if account has >1 health_write within 15m AND writes disagree by >15 points, tag account as "unstable" and route to #cs-unstable for manual review
toni_eng: deploying write-guard hotfix (dry-run=true) to staging now. Plan:
- add compute_ts comparitor on writes
- add canary to 100 accounts
- if green, enable in prod and enable dedupe rule
maya_cs: owners: toni_eng = hotfix + tests, eli_data = export + backfill reconciliation, sam_ops = monitors + suppressor config, me = coordinate CS outreach for any customers already contacted
toni_eng: staging canary looks clean; no overwrites for canary accounts
playbook-bot: pb_health_recalc dedupe_rule flipped to true (dry-run) at 2026-10-11T10:32:10Z
toni_eng: flipping write-guard in prod now (feature=true). will run a short backfill to reconcile any accounts where stored_compute_ts < compute_ts
eli_data: backfill plan: for each affected account, recompute score once (force fresh) and upsert with new compute_ts; emit audit events
eli_data: backfill done for 31 accounts — reconciled scores uploaded: s3://redwood-cs-temp/oscillators_2945123456_reconciled.csv
maya_cs: CS will review reconciled list and mark any customers who received premature outreach; we'll coordinate apologies if needed
sam_ops: un-setting suppressor for stable accounts only; keep suppressor on for ones still flagged unstable
toni_eng: follow-ups: add integration test to prevent async older-job overwrites, add metric alert for health_write_overwrites > 0, and document the race in playbook runbook
maya_cs: filing retro ticket CS-PLAYBOOK-2945 with timeline and remediation steps
playbook-bot: created audit ticket PLAY-2945123456 for postmortem and required tasks
maya_cs: thanks team for fast triage. I'll close this thread and reopen if anything else pops up :thumbsup:
